findings.reason: the plan should name the member's version policy — extend the root's hatch-vcs/git-tag owner (one version for the workspace) — and add the version to the wheel-METADATA check, rather than leave a second version source to be invented at implementation time.
findings.text: the plan states nova-cocos is "built with hatchling like the root" but never states the workspace member's version source, while the root derives its version dynamically from git tags (`dynamic = ["version"]` at pyproject.toml:3, `[tool.hatch.version]` `source = "vcs"` + `version_scheme = "post-release"` at pyproject.toml:161-177); a member given no `[tool.hatch.version]` must hardcode a static version, which makes it a second owner of a number the repo's tags already own and lets the two drift silently, and §1's done-when checks the wheel METADATA only for `Requires-Python` and the absence of `Requires-Dist`, so the drift is unverified.

response_events.reason: v3: s1 names the member's version owner (dynamic version via hatch-vcs over this repository's tags, raw-options at the root, never static) and the done-when checks the wheel Version equals a root build at the same commit.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: v3: s1 names the member's version owner (dynamic version via hatch-vcs over this repository's tags, raw-options at the root, never static) and the done-when checks the wheel Version equals a root build at the same commit.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `packages/nova-cocos/` moves one 224-line module whose small public-name interface (`convention`, `identify_convention`, `transform_factor`, `Convention`, `ConventionTransform`, `TRANSFORMATIONS`, the `*_LIKE` constants) hides the whole factor table and transformation algebra behind it; the plan adds no spread of shallow wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds a new build owner (`packages/nova-cocos/pyproject.toml`) without naming its version source, while the root owns version derivation from git tags via hatch-vcs.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 relocates an existing public surface into `nova_cocos` (no new names) rather than adding to any of the four families, and names the counterpart it retires (`nova/io/cocos.py`, §2).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan's importer census is complete and correct against the tree (4 nova modules, 5 tests, 4 imas-ambix modules) and it cites why no existing installable form exists (nova's 3.14 floor and heavy deps), so the reuse map is present.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only thin layer the plan adds, the `nova/io/cocos.py` re-export, is justified in its own text (imas-ambix's four editable-path imports would break) and the section that retires it is named (§2), which is the justification the item requires.
